title: Fix the Double-Scaled Pointer Arithmetic
description: The program should access the third element of an array using pointer arithmetic.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 30, the third element of the array.
actualProblem: Pointer arithmetic in C already scales by the pointed-to type's size automatically, so p + 2 correctly points 2 ints ahead. Multiplying by sizeof(int) again (p + 2 * sizeof(int)) double-scales the offset, landing far outside the array and reading unrelated (garbage) memory.
explanation: When you write p + n on a typed pointer, C automatically advances the address by n * sizeof(*p) bytes — the scaling by the element size is already built in. Manually multiplying by sizeof() as well applies the scaling twice.
